paragraphs: Ennis, Inc. (collectively with its subsidiaries, the "Company," "Registrant," "Ennis," or "we," "us," or "our") was organized under the laws of Texas in 1909. Ennis is primarily a "trade printer" that manufactures a broad range of printed products that are resold throughout the United States through a network of independent distributors. This distributor channel encompasses independent print distributors, commercial printers, direct mail, fulfillment companies, payroll and accounts payable software companies, and advertising agencies, among others. We also sell products to many of our competitors to satisfy their customers' needs.
Our management believes we are the largest provider of business forms, pressure-seal forms, labels, tags, envelopes, and presentation folders to independent distributors in the United States.

We are in the business of manufacturing, designing and selling business forms and other printed business products primarily to distributors located in the United States. We operate approximately 50 manufacturing plants throughout the United States in 20 strategically located states as one reportable segment; printing services and manufacture of business forms. Approximately 95% of the business products we manufacture are custom and semi-custom products, constructed in a wide variety of sizes, colors, number of parts and quantities on an individual job basis, depending upon the customers' specifications.

The products we sell include snap sets, continuous forms, laser cut sheets, tags, labels, envelopes, integrated products, jumbo rolls and pressure sensitive products in short, medium and long runs under the following labels: Ennis®, Royal Business Forms®, Block Graphics®, ColorWorx®, Enfusion®, Uncompromised Check Solutions®, VersaSeal®, Ad ConceptsSM, FormSource LimitedSM, Star Award Ribbon Company®, Witt Printing®, Genforms®, PrintGraphics®, Calibrated Forms®, PrintXcel®, Printegra®, Forms ManufacturersSM, Mutual Graphics®, TRI-C Business FormsSM, Major Business SystemsSM, Independent PrintingSM, Hayes Graphics®, Wright Business GraphicsSM, Wright 360SM, Integrated Print & GraphicsSM, the Flesh CompanySM, AmeriPrintSM; StylecraftSM, UMC PrintSM; Eagle GraphicsSM, Diamond GraphicsSM, Printing TechnologiesSM and CFC Print & MailSM. We also sell the Adams McClure® brand (which provides Point of Purchase advertising); the Admore®, Folder Express®, and Independent Folders® brands (which provide presentation folders and document folders); Ennis Tag & LabelSM (which provides custom printed, high performance labels and custom and stock tags); Allen-Bailey Tag & LabelSM, Atlas Tag & Label®, Kay Toledo Tag®, and Special Service Partners® (SSP) (which provides custom and stock tags and labels); Trade Envelopes®, Block Graphics®, Wisco®, National Imprint Corporation®, Northeastern Envelope CompanySM, and Envelope SuperstoreSM (which provide custom and imprinted envelopes); Northstar® and General Financial Supply® (which provide financial and security documents); InfosealSM and PrintXcel® (which provide custom and stock pressure seal documents). School Photo Marketing and National School Forms are a one-stop shop for over 1,400 school portrait photographers and professional photo labs nationwide, providing them with a complete array of products and services that reach over 15 million families and 30,000 schools, primarily in the K-8 market. We sell predominantly through independent distributors, as well as to many of our competitors. Northstar Computer Forms, Inc., one of our wholly-owned subsidiaries, also sells direct to a small number of customers, generally large banking organizations (where a distributor is not acceptable or available to the end-user). Adams McClure, LP, a wholly-owned subsidiary, also sells direct to a small number of customers, where sales are generally through advertising agencies.

The printing industry generally sells its products either predominantly to end users, a market dominated by a few large manufacturers, such as R.R. Donnelley and Taylor Corporation, or, like the Company, through a variety of independent distributors and distributor groups. While it is not possible, because of the lack of adequate public statistical information, to determine the Company's share of the total business products market, management believes the Company is the largest producer of business forms, pressure-seal forms, labels, tags, envelopes, and presentation folders in the United States distributing primarily through independent distributors.

There are a number of competitors that operate in this segment. We believe our strategic locations and buying power permit us to compete on a favorable basis within the distributor market on competitive factors, such as service, quality, and price.

Distribution of business forms and other business products throughout the United States is primarily done through independent distributors, including business forms distributors, resellers, direct mail, commercial printers, software companies, and advertising agencies.

Raw materials principally consist of a wide variety of weights, widths, colors, sizes, and qualities of paper for business products purchased primarily from one major supplier at favorable prices based on our high volume of business with that supplier relative to our competitors.

Business products usage in the printing industry is generally not seasonal. General economic conditions and contraction of the traditional business forms industry are the predominant factors in quarterly volume fluctuations.
We have completed a number of acquisitions in recent years.

On November 14, 2025, we acquired the assets and business of CFC Print & Mail ("CFC") in Grand Prairie, Texas. In the last full year preceding the acquisition, CFC generated approximately $7.1 million in sales. The acquisition of CFC further strengthens our leading position in business products and the commercial print sector.

On April 11, 2025, we acquired the assets and business of Northeastern Envelope Company ("NEC") in Old Forge, Pennsylvania, and Envelope Superstore ("ESS") in Hiram, GA. In the last full year preceding the acquisition, NEC and ESS generated approximately $26.9 million in combined sales. The acquisition of NEC and ESS strengthens our envelope converting and printing capabilities to serve our customers in the Northeast United States.

On June 26, 2024, we acquired the assets and business of Printing Technologies, Inc. ("PTI") in Indianapolis, Indiana. In the last full year preceding the acquisition, PTI generated approximately $12.5 million in combined sales. The acquisition of PTI strengthens our production capabilities and diversifies our product offerings to serve our large and growing customer base.
Other than the patent for our VersaSeal® product, we do not have any significant patents, licenses, franchises, or concessions.

headings: Risks related to our business and operations

Our ability to protect our customer relationships, including those acquired through acquisitions, and our trademarks is important to our business, and failure to do so could adversely affect our results of operations.
Digital technologies will continue to erode the demand for our printed business documents.
We obtain our raw materials from a limited number of suppliers, and any disruptions in supply, including the recent closure of a primary supplier's mill, could adversely affect our business.
Challenging financial market conditions and changes in long-term interest rates could adversely impact the funded status of our pension plan.
We may be unable to identify or to complete acquisitions or to successfully integrate the businesses we acquire.
Our distributor customers may be acquired by other manufacturers who redirect business within their plants.
We could experience labor disputes, labor shortages and increases in cost of labor that could disrupt our business in the future and impact operating results.
We face intense competition to gain market share, which may lead some competitors to sell substantial amounts of goods at prices against which we cannot profitably compete.
Environmental regulations may impact our future operating results.
Changes in U.S. tariff and trade policy could adversely affect our business.
We are subject to taxation related risks.
We are exposed to the risk of non-payment by our customers on a significant amount of our sales.
Our business incurs significant freight and transportation costs.
A natural disaster, catastrophe, pandemic or other unexpected events could adversely affect our operations.
We depend on the reliability of our information technology ("IT") and network infrastructure as well as those of third parties. If these systems fail, our operations may be adversely affected.
Increases in the cost of employee benefits could impact our financial results and cash flow.
Risks related to our securities
Because of the volatility in the stock market in general, the market price of our Common Stock will also likely be volatile.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, before making an investment in our common stock. The risks described below are not the only ones we face in our business. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also impair our business operations. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition or operating results could be materially harmed. In such an event, our common stock could decline in price and you may lose all or part of your investment.

We rely on customer relationships, including customer lists obtained through acquisitions, as well as our trade names and trademarks, to support our sales and brand recognition. Although we seek to protect these assets through contractual arrangements, internal controls and trademark registrations, these measures may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized use, disclosure or misappropriation. In addition, we may incur significant costs to enforce our rights, and such efforts may not be successful. Any loss of customer information, or inability to maintain, protect or enforce our trade names and trademarks, could result in loss of customers, reputational harm and reduced revenues.

Our results and financial condition are affected by global and local market conditions, competitors' pricing strategies, including the impact of tariffs and trade policies, which can adversely affect our sales, margins, and net income.

Our results of operations can be affected by local, national and worldwide market conditions. The consequences of domestic and international economic uncertainty or instability, volatility in commodity markets, and domestic or international policy uncertainty, all of which we have seen in the past, can all impact economic activity. Unfavorable conditions can depress the demand for our products and thus sales in a given market and may prompt competitor's pricing strategies that adversely affect our margins or constrain our operating flexibility. Certain macroeconomic events, such as crises in the financial markets, inflation, high interest rates, tariffs, recessionary concerns, cost and labor pressures, distribution challenges and the availability of paper could have a more wide-ranging and prolonged impact on the general business environment, which could also adversely affect us. Whether we can manage these risks effectively depends on several factors, including (i) our ability to manage movements in commodity prices and the impact of government actions to manage national economic conditions such as consumer spending, inflation rates and unemployment levels, particularly given the past volatility in the global financial markets, (ii) the impact on our margins of labor costs given our labor-intensive business model, the trend toward higher wages in both mature and developing markets and the potential impact of union organizing efforts on day-to-day operations of our manufacturing facilities and (iii) other factors, which may be beyond our control.

The printing industry continues to experience weakening demand for printed products. The increasing sophistication of software, internet technologies, and digital equipment combined with our customers' general preference, digital workflow, automation and electronic alternatives as well as governmental influences for paperless business environments will continue to reduce the number of traditional printed documents sold. Moreover, the documents that will continue to coexist with software applications will likely contain less value-added print content.

Increasing postal rates make direct mail campaigns more expensive, potentially leading our customers to reduce their demand for our products and shift to alternative marketing channels. Many of our custom-printed documents help companies control their internal business processes and facilitate the flow of information. These applications will increasingly be conducted over the internet or through other electronic payment systems. The predominant method of our customers' communication with their customers is by printed information. As their customers become more accepting of internet communications, our customers may increasingly opt for what is perceived to be a less costly electronic option, which would reduce our revenue. The pace of these trends is difficult to predict. These factors will tend to reduce the industry-wide demand for printed documents and require us to gain market share to maintain or increase our current level of print-based revenue which could place pressure on our operating margins.

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis provides material historical and prospective disclosures intended to enable investors and other users to assess our financial condition and results of operations. Statements that are not historical are forward-looking and involve risk and uncertainties, including those discussed under the caption "Risk Factors" in Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K and elsewhere in this Report. You should read this discussion and analysis in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and the related notes appearing elsewhere in this Report. The words "anticipate," "preliminary," "expect," "believe," "intend" and similar expressions identify forward-looking statements. We believe these forward-looking statements are based upon reasonable assumptions. All such statements involve risks and uncertainties, and as a result, actual results could differ materially from those projected, anticipated, or implied by these statements.

In view of such uncertainties, investors should not place undue reliance on our forward-looking statements since such statements may prove to be inaccurate and speak only as of the date when made. We undertake no obligation to publicly update or revise any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise.

This Management's Discussion and Analysis covers the continuing operations of the Company, which are comprised of the production and sale of business forms and other business products. This Management's Discussion and Analysis includes the following sections:

• Overview – An overall discussion regarding our Company, the business challenges and opportunities we believe are key to our success, and our plans for facing these challenges relating to our continuing operations.

• Critical Accounting Estimates – A discussion of the accounting policies that require our most critical judgments and estimates relating to our continuing operations. This discussion provides insight into the level of subjectivity, quality, and variability involved in these judgments and estimates. This section also provides a summary of recently adopted and recently issued accounting pronouncements that have or may materially affect our business.

• Results of Operations – An analysis of our consolidated results of operations and segment results for the three years presented in our Consolidated Financial Statements. This analysis discusses material trends within our continuing business and provides important information necessary for an understanding of our continuing operating results.

• Liquidity and Capital Resources – An analysis of our cash flows and a discussion of our financial condition and contractual obligations. This section provides information necessary to evaluate our ability to generate cash and to meet existing and known future cash requirements over both the short and long term.
References to 2026, 2025 and 2024 refer to the fiscal years ended February 28, 2026, February 28, 2025 and February 29, 2024, respectively.

Our Business Challenges – Our industry continues to experience consolidation of traditional supply channels, ongoing product obsolescence, paper supplier capacity adjustments, and periodic pricing volatility and potential supply allocations resulting from demand and supply imbalance. Technology advances have enabled electronic document distribution, web-based hosting, digital printing and print-on-demand as viable and cost-effective alternatives to traditional custom-printed documents and customer communications. Improved equipment has become more accessible to both existing and new competitors. As a result, we face highly competitive conditions in an already mature, price-competitive print industry.
In addition to the risk factors discussed under the caption "Risk Factors" in Item 1A of this Annual Report, some of the key challenges of our business include the following:

Transformation of our portfolio of products – While traditional business documents remain essential to conducting business, many are being replaced through the use of lower-cost paper grades or imported products, or are being devalued by advances in digital technologies, resulting in continued declines in demand for a portion of our product line. Transforming our product offerings in order to provide innovative, value-added solutions on a proactive basis requires ongoing investments in new and existing technologies, as well as the development of key strategic business relationships, including print-on-demand services and product offerings that support customers transitioning to digital business environments. We continue to evaluate new market opportunities and niches, including through acquisitions, and to expand our offerings in areas such as envelopes, tags, folders, healthcare wristbands, specialty packaging, direct mail, pressure seal products, secure document, in-mold labels, and long-run integrated high color web print, which provide opportunities for growth and further differentiate us from our competition. Our ability to make such investments or pursue acquisitions is dependent on our liquidity, capital resources, and operating results.

Production capacity and price competition within our industry – Industry supply of paper products continues to fluctuate as changing market conditions influence producers to idle or permanently close individual machines or mills, or convert capacity to alternative product lines, including packaging, to offset declines in demand for certain paper grades. Recent industry activity has included temporary idling of machines, permanent closures and limited increases in specialty paper capacity, reflecting ongoing adjustments in response to shifts in demand. During the current fiscal year, the only domestic producer of carbonless paper permanently closed its mill which has contributed to ongoing supply constraints for this product. As previously reported, we increased inventory levels to provide buffer stock while transitioning to alternative sources of carbonless paper.

These dynamics may result in continued supply constraints and input cost volatility for certain paper grades. Margins remain under pressure due to volume variability in certain markets, elevated input costs and ongoing pricing competition. To mitigate these impacts, we continue to manage product costs through forecasting, production and costing models, strengthening supplier relationships; negotiating procurement terms; and improving operational efficiency, while evaluating opportunities to better leverage our fixed cost structure.

Continued consolidation of our customers – Our customers are primarily distributors, many of which are consolidating or are being acquired by competitors. While we have historically maintained a significant share of business with these customers, continued consolidation may affect our sales volume, pricing, and margins.

paragraphs: Ennis, Inc. (包含其子公司在內，簡稱為 "Company," "Registrant," "Ennis," 或 "we," "us," 或 "our") 於1909年根據德克薩斯州法律設立。Ennis 主要為一間 "貿易印刷廠"，製造廣泛的印刷產品，並透過獨立經銷商網路銷售至美國各地。此經銷商渠道包含獨立印刷經銷商、商業印刷廠、直郵服務、履行服務公司、薪資與應付款軟體公司以及廣告代理商等。我們也銷售產品給許多競爭對手，以滿足其客戶的需求。
我們的管理階層認為，我們是美國獨立經銷商市場中，提供商業用紙、壓力封口紙、標籤、標籤、信封與展示文件的最大供應商。
我們的業務為製造、設計與銷售商業用紙及其他印刷商業產品，主要銷售給位於美國的經銷商。我們在美國約有50間製造廠，分佈於20個戰略位置的州，作為一個應報告分部運作；印刷服務與商業用紙製造。我們製造的商業產品中，約有95%為客製化與半客製化產品，根據客戶的規格，以個別訂單方式製造，包含多種尺寸、顏色、零件數與數量。

我們銷售的產品包括快接套件、連續紙、雷射裁切紙、標籤、標籤、信封、整合產品、大卷紙與壓力敏感產品，以短、中、長版印刷方式銷售，並使用以下品牌標籤：Ennis®, Royal Business Forms®, Block Graphics®, ColorWorx®, Enfusion®, Uncompromised Check Solutions®, VersaSeal®, Ad ConceptsSM, FormSource LimitedSM, Star Award Ribbon Company®, Witt Printing®, Genforms®, PrintGraphics®, Calibrated Forms®, PrintXcel®, Printegra®, Forms ManufacturersSM, Mutual Graphics®, TRI-C Business FormsSM, Major Business SystemsSM, Independent PrintingSM, Hayes Graphics®, Wright Business GraphicsSM, Wright 360SM, Integrated Print & GraphicsSM, the Flesh CompanySM, AmeriPrintSM; StylecraftSM, UMC PrintSM; Eagle GraphicsSM, Diamond GraphicsSM, Printing TechnologiesSM and CFC Print & MailSM。我們也銷售 Adams McClure® 品牌（提供零售點廣告）；Admore®, Folder Express®, 和 Independent Folders® 品牌（提供展示文件與文件文件）；Ennis Tag & LabelSM（提供客製印刷、高性能標籤與客製與現成標籤）；Allen-Bailey Tag & LabelSM, Atlas Tag & Label®, Kay Toledo Tag®, 和 Special Service Partners® (SSP)（提供客製與現成標籤與標籤）；Trade Envelopes®, Block Graphics®, Wisco®, National Imprint Corporation®, Northeastern Envelope CompanySM, 和 Envelope SuperstoreSM（提供客製與印刷信封）；Northstar® 和 General Financial Supply®（提供財務與安全文件）；InfosealSM 和 PrintXcel®（提供客製與現成壓力封口文件）。School Photo Marketing 和 National School Forms 是一個一站式服務，為全美超過1,400間學校肖像攝影師與專業相片實驗室提供完整產品與服務，服務超過15百萬家庭與30,000間學校，主要為K-8市場。我們主要透過獨立經銷商銷售，同時也銷售給許多競爭對手。Northstar Computer Forms, Inc.，我們的一家 wholly-owned 子公司，也直接銷售給少數客戶，通常為大型銀行機構（在終端用戶無法接受或取得經銷商的情況下）。Adams McClure, LP，我們的一家 wholly-owned 子公司，也直接銷售給少數客戶，通常透過廣告代理商進行銷售。
印刷業通常將其產品主要銷售給終端用戶，此市場由少數大型製造商主導，例如 R.R. Donnelley 和 Taylor Corporation，或，如同本公司，透過多種獨立經銷商與經銷商羣體進行銷售。雖然無法確定本公司在總商業產品市場的佔有率，因為缺乏足夠的公開統計資料，但管理階層認為本公司是美國最大的商業用紙、壓力封口紙、標籤、標籤、信封與展示文件供應商，主要透過獨立經銷商進行銷售。
此段落中存在許多競爭對手。我們認為，我們的戰略位置與採購實力，使我們能在經銷商市場中，以有利的條件競爭，競爭因素包括服務、品質與價格。
商業用紙及其他商業產品在美國的分銷，主要透過獨立經銷商進行，包括商業用紙經銷商、經銷商、直郵服務、商業印刷廠、軟體公司與廣告代理商。
原材料主要為各種重量、寬度、顏色、尺寸與品質的紙張，用於商業產品，主要從一家主要供應商處購入，價格優渥，這是因為我們與該供應商的業務量遠高於競爭對手。
印刷業的業務產品使用通常不具季節性。總體經濟狀況及傳統商業形式產業的收縮，是每季銷售量波動的主要因素。
我們近年已完成數筆收購。
於 2025 年 11 月 14 日，我們取得位於德州格蘭德普雷的 CFC Print & Mail（"CFC"）的資產與業務。在收購前的最後完整會計年度，CFC 產生約 7.1 百萬美元的銷售額。取得 CFC 進一步強化我們在業務產品及商業印刷領域的領導地位。

於 2025 年 4 月 11 日，我們取得位於賓州奧爾德福爾的 Northeastern Envelope Company（"NEC"）及位於喬治亞州希拉姆的 Envelope Superstore（"ESS"）的資產與業務。在收購前的最後完整會計年度，NEC 與 ESS 合計產生約 26.9 百萬美元的銷售額。取得 NEC 與 ESS 有助於強化我們在信封轉換與印刷能力，以服務美國東北部的客戶。
於 2024 年 6 月 26 日，我們取得位於印第安那州印第安納波利斯的 Printing Technologies, Inc.（"PTI"）的資產與業務。在收購前的最後完整會計年度，PTI 合計產生約 12.5 百萬美元的銷售額。取得 PTI 有助於強化我們的生產能力，並拓展我們的產品組合，以服務我們龐大的成長中的客戶羣。
除了我們 VersaSeal® 產品的專利外，我們沒有任何重要的專利、授權、特許經營或特許權。

paragraphs: 本管理層討論與分析提供重要的歷史與展望性資訊，旨在協助投資人及其他使用者評估本公司的財務狀況與營運成果。非歷史性陳述為展望性陳述，並涉及風險與不確定性，包括在本年度報告表 10-K 第 1A 項「風險因素」標題下以及本報告其他部分所討論的風險因素。請配合本公司合併財務報表及相關附註閱讀本討論與分析。詞彙如「預期」、「初步」、「預期」、「相信」、「意圖」等，用以識別展望性陳述。本公司認為這些展望性陳述是基於合理的假設。所有這些陳述均涉及風險與不確定性，因此實際結果可能與這些陳述所預測、預期或暗示的結果有重大差異。
考慮到這些不確定性，投資人不應過度依賴本公司的展望性陳述，因為這些陳述可能被證明不正確，且僅反映陳述當日的情況。本公司不負有公開更新或修正任何展望性陳述的義務，無論是因新資訊、未來事件或其他原因。
本管理層討論與分析涵蓋本公司的持續營運，其內容包括業務形式及其他業務產品的生產與銷售。本管理層討論與分析包含以下各節：
• 總覽 – 關於本公司、我們認為對成功至關重要的業務挑戰與機會，以及我們面對這些挑戰的計畫，進行整體討論。
• 關鍵會計估計 – 討論涉及我們持續營運最關鍵判斷與估計的會計政策。此討論提供對這些判斷與估計所涉及的主觀性、品質與變動性的見解。此節也提供最近採用與發佈的會計準則摘要，這些準則可能或已對本公司業務產生重大影響。
• 營運成果 – 分析我們合併營運成果與分部營運成果，針對本合併財務報表中所列示的三個會計年度。此分析討論我們持續業務中的重要趨勢，並提供理解我們持續營運成果所必需的重要資訊。
• 流動性與資本資源 – 分析我們的現金流量，並討論我們的財務狀況與契約義務。此節提供評估我們產生現金能力與滿足現有及已知未來現金需求的資訊，包括短期與長期。
提及 2026 年、2025 年與 2024 年，是指財務年度分別為 2026 年 2 月 28 日、2025 年 2 月 28 日與 2024 年 2 月 29 日。
我們的業務挑戰 – 我們的產業持續面臨傳統供應鏈的整併、持續的產品淘汰、紙張供應商產能調整，以及因需求與供應失衡而產生的週期性價格波動與潛在供應分配。科技進步已使電子文件分發、基於網頁的存放、數位印刷與按需印刷成為傳統客製印刷文件與客戶溝通的可行且成本效益更高的替代方案。改善的設備已變得對現有與新進競爭者更加容易取得。因此，我們在一個已經成熟的、價格競爭激烈的印刷產業中面臨高度競爭的環境。
除了在本年度報告第 1A 項「風險因素」標題下討論的風險因素外，我們業務的一些關鍵挑戰包括以下內容：

我們產品組合的轉型 – 雖然傳統業務文件仍是進行業務的必要工具，但許多文件正被較低成本的紙張等級或進口產品取代，或因數位科技的進步而價值降低，導致我們產品線中一部分的產品需求持續下降。為提供創新且具附加價值的解決方案，我們必須持續投資於新舊技術，並建立關鍵的戰略性商業關係，包括按需印刷服務與支持客戶轉型至數位業務環境的產品。我們持續評估新的市場機會與利基市場，包括透過收購，並擴展我們在信封、標籤、摺疊盒、醫療腕帶、特殊包裝、直郵、壓力封口產品、安全文件、內模標籤與長跑整合高色彩網印等領域的產品線，這些領域提供成長機會並進一步區隔我們與競爭對手。我們是否有能力進行這些投資或進行收購，取決於我們的流動性、資本資源與營運成果。

生產能力與產業內的價格競爭 – 紙張產品的產業供應持續波動，因市場條件的變化影響生產商閒置或永久關閉個別機臺或紙廠，或轉換至替代產品線，包括包裝，以彌補某些紙張等級需求的下降。近期產業活動包括機臺暫時閒置、永久關閉與特殊紙張產能有限增加，反映持續調整以應對需求變動。在當前會計年度，唯一國內碳素紙生產商永久關閉其紙廠，這已導致該產品的供應限制持續存在。如先前報導，我們已提高存貨水準，以提供緩衝庫存，同時轉向替代的碳素紙來源。
這些動態可能導致某些紙張等級持續出現供應限制與投入成本波動。毛利率因某些市場的銷量變動、投入成本上升與持續的價格競爭而受到壓力。為緩解這些影響，我們持續透過預測、生產與成本模型來管理產品成本，強化供應商關係；談判採購條款；並提升營運效率，同時評估機會以更有效地運用我們的固定成本結構。
我們客戶的持續整併 – 我們的客戶主要是經銷商，其中許多正在整併或被競爭對手收購。雖然我們歷來在這些客戶中維持相當大的業務份額，但持續的整併可能影響我們的銷售量、價格與毛利率。

headings: 與本公司業務及營運相關之風險
本公司保護客戶關係，包括透過併購所取得之客戶關係，以及本公司商標之能力，對本公司業務至關重要，未能妥善保護可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
數位科技將持續削弱本公司印刷業務文件之需求。
本公司從有限數量之供應商取得原物料，若供應鏈發生中斷，包括近期主要供應商廠區關閉，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
困難之財務市場環境及長期利率之變動，可能對本公司退休金計畫之資金狀況造成不利影響。
本公司可能無法識別或完成併購，或成功整合所取得之業務。
本公司經銷商客戶可能被其他製造商收購，並在其廠內重新導向業務。
本公司可能遭遇勞資爭議、勞動力短缺及勞動成本增加，這些情況可能未來幹擾本公司業務並影響營運成果。
我們面臨激烈的競爭以爭取市場佔有率，這可能導致部分競爭對手以我們無法有利可圖競爭的價格銷售大量商品。
環境法規可能影響我們未來的營運成果。
美國關稅與貿易政策的變動可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們面臨與稅務相關的風險。
我們面臨客戶未支付我們重大銷售額的風險。
我們的業務產生顯著的運輸與運費成本。
天然災害、災難、疫情或其他未預期事件可能對我們的營運產生不利影響。
我們依賴資訊科技（"IT"）與網路基礎建設及其第三方的可靠性。若這些系統失敗，可能對我們的營運產生不利影響。
員工福利成本的增加可能影響本公司的財務結果及現金流。
與本公司證券相關的風險
由於股票市場總體波動性，本公司普通股的市場價格也將可能出現波動。
paragraphs: 您應仔細審閱下列所列風險，以及本年度報表 10-K 所包含或參考的其他資訊，再做投資本公司普通股的決定。下列所列風險並非本公司在營運中所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知或認為不重要，也可能影響本公司營運。若任何下列風險發生，將可能對本公司營運、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大損害。在此情況下，本公司普通股的價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。
我們依賴客戶關係，包括透過收購所取得的客戶名單，以及我們的商標與商號，來支撐我們的銷售與品牌認知。雖然我們透過契約安排、內部控制與商標登記來保護這些資產，但這些措施可能無法完全防止未經授權的使用、洩漏或侵佔。此外，我們可能需承擔重大成本來執行我們的權利，且這些努力可能無法成功。若發生客戶資訊遺失，或無法維持、保護或執行我們的商標與商號，將可能導致客戶流失、聲譽受損與營收減少。
我們的營運成果與財務狀況受全球與地方市場條件、競爭對手的價格策略，包括關稅與貿易政策的影響，這些因素可能對我們的銷售、毛利率與淨收入造成不利影響。

我們的營運成果可能受地方、國家與全球市場條件的影響。國內與國際經濟不確定性或不穩定性、商品市場波動，以及國內或國際政策不確定性，這些我們過去曾見過的情況，都可能影響經濟活動。不利的條件可能壓抑我們產品的需求，進而影響特定市場的銷售，並可能促使競爭對手調整價格策略，對我們的毛利率或營運彈性造成不利影響。某些總體經濟事件，例如金融市場危機、通貨膨脹、高利率、經濟衰退的擔憂、成本與勞動壓力、分銷挑戰以及紙張的可得性，可能對整體營商環境產生更廣泛且延長的影響，這也可能對我們造成不利影響。我們能否有效管理這些風險，取決於多種因素，包括（i）我們管理商品價格變動的能力，以及政府行動對國家經濟條件的影響，例如消費支出、通貨膨脹率與失業率，特別是考慮到過去全球金融市場的波動性；（ii）勞動成本對我們毛利率的影響，由於我們的勞動密集型營運模式，成熟與發展中市場的工資趨勢上揚，以及工會組織活動對我們製造廠日常營運的潛在影響；（iii）其他因素，這些因素可能超出我們的控制範圍。
印刷業持續面臨印刷產品需求下降的壓力。軟體、互聯網技術與數位設備的日益進步，加上客戶普遍偏好數位工作流程、自動化與電子選項，以及政府推動無紙化營運環境，將持續減少傳統印刷文件的銷售數量。此外，未來與軟體應用共存的文件，很可能包含較少的附加價值印刷內容。

郵資上漲使直接郵件行銷活動成本增加，可能導致客戶減少對我們產品的需求，並轉向其他行銷渠道。我們許多客製化印刷文件協助企業控制內部營運流程，並促進資訊流動。這些應用將越來越透過互聯網或其他電子付款系統進行。我們客戶與其客戶的主要溝通方式為印刷資訊。隨著其客戶對互聯網溝通的接受度提高，客戶可能越來越傾向選擇被視為較低成本的電子選項，這將減少我們的營收。這些趨勢的發展速度難以預測。這些因素將傾向於降低整個產業對印刷文件的需求，並要求我們爭取市場佔有率以維持或提高目前的印刷營收水平，這可能對我們的營運毛利率造成壓力。
